body.statement: Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 states that, for an \(F\)-identifiability tuple \(\langle G,V,C_V,W\rangle\), functionally eliminating any set of observed functional variables that are neither treatments nor outcomes, are separable from \(C_V\), and have observed parents preserves \(F\)-identifiability of the causal effect of \(X\) on \(Y\).

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 15. Let ⟨G, V, C_V, W⟩ be an F-identifiability tuple. Let Z be a set of observed functional variables that are neither treatments nor outcomes, are separable from C_V, and that have observed parents. If G′ is the result of functionally eliminating variables Z from G, then the causal effect of X on Y is F-identifiable wrt ⟨G, V, C_V, W⟩ iff it is F-identifiable wrt ⟨G′, V \ Z, C_V, W \ Z⟩.

attestation.note: Verified by mill-w03 against the official NeurIPS 2024 proceedings PDF, theorem printed across PDF pages 8-9 (paper pages 7-8), downloaded 2026-09-10.
